nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طسۤ تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these are ﴿آيَاتُ ٱلْقُرْآنِ﴾ which you were promised.
﴿وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾ i.e. and the verses of a clear Book.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: i.e. We made this their recompense for disbelief.
And it was said: i.e. We made obedience and faith attractive to them, because they are among the deeds of creatures.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: so they waver to and fro in error.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى ٱلْقُرْآنَ مِن لَّدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾.
i.e. it is cast upon you, and you receive it.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لأَهْلِهِ إِنِّيۤ آنَسْتُ نَاراً﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. I perceived (saw).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And from it is said: ins (humankind), because they are visible. [Translator's note: the source reads ومن قيل; read ومنه قيل.]
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَآتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-shihāb is fire.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: Everything that has light is called shihāb.
Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā (Thaʿlab) said: The origin of al-shihāb is a stick at one of whose ends is a live coal, while the other has no fire in it. Al-jadhwa is likewise, except that it is thicker than the shihāb; and it is called jadhwa because it is the stump of the tree as it is.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says: قَبَسْتُ النَّارَ أقْبِسُها قَبْساً (I took a brand of fire), and the noun is al-qabas.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلِونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They were in winter, and they had lost the way.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾.
i.e. when Mūsā came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it."
ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The fire is the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He called Mūsā ﷺ while he was in the light; ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ are the angels."
Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda narrated from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb: The fire is the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ is Mūsā and the angels ﷺ.
And it was said: ﴿مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾ are the angels charged with it,
and ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ are also the angels.
And the meaning is: they say "Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
Ibn Abī [Translator's note: the name is cut short in the source; presumably Ibn Abī Najīḥ] narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾: and he did not turn back.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنِّي لاَ يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ. إَلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ﴾.
There are several statements about its meaning:
a- Among them that there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: In My presence the messengers do not fear; only others fear, of those who did wrong. ﴿إلاَّ مَنْ ظَلَم﴾ and then repented — he does not fear.
b- And it was said: the meaning is: In My presence the messengers do not fear; but whoever did wrong, of the messengers and others, and then repented, does not fear.
c- And it was said: ﴿إِلاَّ﴾ has the meaning of the wāw (and); but this is not good in Arabic.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ﴾.
The meaning is: and draw it out, it will come out white.
Miqsam narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ﴾ — without leprosy.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ﴾.
The meaning is: of nine signs; and "في" has the meaning of "مِنْ" because of its closeness to it, as you say: "Take for me ten camels, among them (فيها) two stallions", i.e. of them. And al-Aṣmaʿī said about the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وهلْ يَنْعَمَنْ مَنْ كَانَ آخِرُ عَهْدِهِ * ثلاثينَ شَهْراً في ثَلاثَةِ أَحْوَالِ
(Can one live happily whose latest acquaintance [with the place] was thirty months ago, in [i.e. out of] three years?)
"في" has the meaning of "مِنْ"; and it may have the meaning of "مع" (with).
The meaning is: and throw your staff, and put your hand into your bosom — two signs of nine signs.
And the nine signs, according to what is narrated, are: "the staff becoming a serpent, his hand being white without blemish, the drought that struck them in their open country, the shortage of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ﴾.
(i.e.) it will come out white (as a sign) to Pharaoh and his people.
And it was said: the meaning is: (you are) sent and dispatched to Pharaoh and his people; this is the statement of al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ آيَاتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً﴾.
i.e. clear.
And ﴿مُبْصِرَةً﴾ [Translator's note: the source repeats the same vocalisation; the variant meant is probably مُبْصَرَة] i.e. made clear.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَحَدُواْ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْماً وَعُلُوّاً﴾.
i.e. out of arrogance that they should believe in Mūsā ﷺ, when he had brought them the proofs and the signs.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَانُ دَاوُودَ﴾.
It is the way of a son to inherit from his father, so the point here is that it is an inheritance of knowledge and of taking charge of people's affairs; and from this is: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets."
It is narrated that Dāwūd, peace be upon him, had nineteen sons, and Sulaymān inherited prophethood and kingship from him to the exclusion of them. ﴿وَقَالَ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
i.e. of everything that prophets and people are given.
This is by way of expressing abundance, as one says: "I left no one without speaking to him about your affair."

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: the first of them are held back for the last of them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of وَزَعْتُه is "I restrained him"; and from it: people must have restrainers (wazaʿa); and from it: "What the ruler restrains is more than what the Qurʾān restrains."
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَهُمْ يُوْزَعُونَ﴾ — he said: Over every kind of them there were restrainers, who held back the first of them for the last of them, so that they would not go ahead in the march, as kings do.
This is a clear statement; and from it: وَزَع فلانٌ فلاناً عن الظُّلمِ, when he restrained him from wrongdoing, as al-Nābigha said:
عَلَى حِينِ عَاتَبْتُ المَشِيبَ عَلَى الصِّبَا * وقلتُ: أَلَمَّا يَصْحُ؟ وَالشَّيْبُ وَازِعُ
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful folly, and said: Has [the heart] not yet sobered? — and grey hair is a restrainer.)

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمْلِ﴾.
It is narrated that it was a valley in Syria whose ants were the size of flies.
Sulaymān al-Taymī read: ﴿يَا أَيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلْوا مَسَاكِنَكُنَّ لا يَحْطِمنكُنَّ سُلَيْمانُ بجنودِهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكاً مِّن قَوْلِهَا﴾.
And it is read ﴿فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَحِكَاً مِنْ قَوْلِهَا﴾; and it is said: such is the laughter of the prophets.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِيۤ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ﴾.
The exegetes said: ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ﴾ i.e. inspire me; and it is taken from the former (meaning), i.e. restrain me from things except from thanking for Your favour, i.e. restrain me from what distances (me) from You.

nahhas-meani:20-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَالِيَ لاَ أَرَى ٱلْهُدْهُدَ﴾ [verse 20].
Abū Mijlaz said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: I want to ask you about three questions. He said: Do you ask me while you recite the Qurʾān?
He said: Yes — three times.
He said: Why did Sulaymān look for the hoopoe rather than the rest of the birds?
He said: He needed water and did not know its depth — or he said: its distance — and the hoopoe knew that, unlike the other birds, so he looked for it.
And elsewhere, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that "Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq" said to him: How can this be, when a boy can trap it? Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: When the decree comes, the sight is blinded.
ʿAṭāʾ said: Mujāhid narrated to us from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Sulaymān would sit, and couches would be placed before him. He would command the humans and they would sit on them, then he would command the jinn and they would sit behind them, then he would command the devils and they would sit behind them. Then the birds would shade them, and the wind would carry them a month's journey, and its evening course was a month. Then he looked for the hoopoe among the birds and said ﴿لأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذَاباً شَدِيداً﴾."
And his punishing it would have been plucking it and throwing it on the ground, unable to protect itself from an ant or a crawling creature.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād said: "His punishing it would have been to pluck it and throw it in the sun."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّي بِسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
i.e. with a clear proof.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
i.e. not a long time.
The implied form is: Sulaymān waited not long, from when he asked about the hoopoe until the hoopoe came; ﴿فَقَال﴾ i.e. the hoopoe said, when Sulaymān asked it about its absence: ﴿أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: then it came, and Sulaymān asked it about its absence, ﴿فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ﴾.
The meaning of "I encompassed the thing" is: I knew it from all its sides.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ﴾.
It was said: "Sabaʾ" is the name of a man.
And it was said: it is a city near Yemen.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنِّي وَجَدتُّ ٱمْرَأَةً تَمْلِكُهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: She was a woman called "Bilqīs", daughter of Sharāḥīl; one of her parents was of the jinn, and the back of her foot was like a donkey's hoof.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.
i.e. of everything that the like of her is given.
﴿وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ i.e. a large throne, of great value.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ للَّهِ﴾.
It is "أن" with "لا" entering upon it.
And the meaning is: so that they do not prostrate to Allah.
And it may be that "أن" is a badal (substitute) for "أعمالهم".
Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read ﴿أَلاَ يَا اسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ﴾.
The meaning according to this reading is: "Lo! O you (people), prostrate to Allah", as the poet said:
يَا لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ والأَقْوَامِ كلِّهِمِ * والصَّالِحينَ على سَمْعَانَ من جَارِ
(O [people], the curse of Allah and of all peoples and of the righteous be upon Samʿān as a neighbour!)
So the meaning is: O you, the curse of Allah (be upon …).
According to this reading it is a place of prostration (sajda), and according to the first reading it is not a place of prostration, because the meaning is: and Satan made it attractive to them not to prostrate to Allah.
The speech according to the first reading is coherent, while according to the second reading something has been interposed in the speech that is not part of it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ٱلَّذِي يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Ibn (Abī) Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿الخَبءُ﴾ is what is hidden. [Translator's note: the source reads ابن نجيح.]
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿الخبءُ﴾ is the secret.
And it was said: al-khabʾ in the heavens is the rain, and in the earth the plants.
The first — what is hidden in the heavens and the earth — is more fitting, and His saying ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا يُخْفُونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ indicates it.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَابِي هَـٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنْظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
It was said: the meaning is: cast it to them, and see what they return, then turn away from them.
And it was said: He only taught it the etiquette of kings, i.e. cast it to them and do not stand waiting, but turn away and then come back.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلأُ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: so it went and cast it to them, and heard her saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلأُ إِنِّيۤ أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ كِتَابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
It was said: She said ﴿كريم﴾ (noble) because of the nobility and eminence of its sender.
And it was said: because it was sealed.
And it was said: She said ﴿كريم﴾ because of what was in it; and in it was: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From the servant of Allah Sulaymān to Bilqīs: ﴿ألاَّ تَعْلُوا عليَّ وائْتُوني مُسْلِمين﴾." The letters of the prophets were concise, and people followed this model: "From the servant of Allah…".
ʿĀṣim said, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The Prophet ﷺ wrote (headings of) four (kinds of) letters. He used to write "In Your name, O Allah"; when ﴿بسم الله مَجْرِيهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا﴾ was revealed, he wrote "In the name of Allah"; when ﴿قل ادْعُوا اللهَ أو ادْعُوْا الرَّحْمَنَ﴾ was revealed, he wrote "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful"; and when ﴿إنَّهُ من سُلَيْمانَ وَإنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحيِمِ﴾ was revealed, he wrote "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate".
ʿĀṣim said: I said to al-Shaʿbī: I have seen a letter of the Prophet ﷺ in which is ﴿بِسمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحيِمِ﴾. He said: That is the third letter.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاَّ تَعْلُواْ عَلَيَّ وَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾.
i.e. that you not be arrogant.
And it may be that the meaning is: (it is) that you not exalt yourselves against me, i.e. he wrote (commanding) the abandonment of haughtiness.
And it is permissible, according to the school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, that "أن" have the meaning of "أي" (namely), explicative, as He said ﴿وَانْطَلقَ المَلأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا﴾.
And it may be that the meaning is: there has been cast to me (the command) that you not exalt yourselves against me.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُواْ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا﴾.
i.e. when they enter it by force.
Every city in which people gather is called qarya, from قَرَيْتُ الشَّيءَ, i.e. I gathered the thing.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلُوۤاْ أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَآ أَذِلَّةً وَكَذٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
It may be that ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ is from the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And it may be from her speech.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: She sent boys dressed in girls' clothing, and girls dressed in boys' clothing.
Yaʿlā ibn Muslim narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: She sent two hundred young slaves, male and female, and said: If he is a prophet, he will distinguish the males from the females. So he ordered them to perform ablution; whoever of them performed ablution beginning with the elbow before the hand, he said: This is one of the females; and whoever began with the hand before the elbow, he said: This is one of the males.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it was said: She sent him a brick of gold in a piece of silk; so Sulaymān ﷺ ordered bricks of gold, and they were thrown beneath the animals until they trampled them.
This fits better with his saying ﴿أَتُمِدُّوْنَنِي بِمَالٍ﴾?
And it may be that she sent both together.
The meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لاَ قِبَلَ لَهُمْ بِهَا﴾ is: they cannot bear them and cannot stand firm against them.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ قَالَ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلأُ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾.
It was said: Sulaymān only said this because, once they had submitted (become Muslims), it would not be lawful for him to take anything of theirs.
And it was said: He only wanted to display a miraculous sign by that.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِّن ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ﴾.
Abū Rajāʾ read: ﴿قال عِفْرِيَةٌ﴾, with the yāʾ vowelled.
Qatāda said: It is the cunning one.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One who is strong and has malice and cunning is called ʿifr, ʿifriya, ʿifrīt and ʿufāriya; and it was said: ʿifrīt means a chief.
Wahb said: The ʿifrīt's name was "Kawdhan".
His saying ﴿أَنَاْ آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ﴾, i.e. from your session in which you judge between the people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says maqām and maqāma for the place in which one stands.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلَّذِي عِندَهُ عِلْمٌ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
There are several statements on the meaning of this:
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: He knew the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which, when He is called upon by it, He answers; and it is "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour".
Someone else said: His name was "Āṣaf ibn Barkhiyā", and he was of the Children of Israel; this is one statement.
And it was said: The one who had knowledge of the Book was "Sulaymān" himself: when the jinnī said to him ﴿أنا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ تَقُومَ من مَقامِكَ﴾ and claimed something — which it would be unlikely for the like of him (to do) — Sulaymān said to him: I will bring it to you in a time nearer than this, by the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided that we destroy it and you restore it to this place of ours, before you blink.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: It was Jibrīl, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
And regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾,
there are also two statements:
1- Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: He raised his gaze, then lowered it, and there was the throne.
2- Mujāhid said: before the stretching of the gaze (to its farthest extent).
Then Mujāhid said: (a distance) like that between us and al-Ḥīra — and he was at that time in Kūfa, among Kinda.
Those who said that the speaker of this was "Sulaymān" adduced His saying ﴿قَالَ هَذَا مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي﴾ to the end of the verse.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād said: The throne appeared from a tunnel beneath the earth.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا نَنظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِيۤ﴾.
i.e. alter it.
It was said: its top was made its bottom, and its bottom its top.
Qatāda said: ﴿نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا﴾ — alter it by adding or removing.
﴿نَنْظُر أتهتدي﴾ — Mujāhid said: i.e. will she recognise it?

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قِيلَ أَهَكَذَا عَرْشُكِ؟ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ﴾.
Qatāda said: She likened it to it, because she had left it behind her when she set out.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَأُوتِينَا ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Sulaymān, peace be upon him, says it.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. her disbelief.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to this is: and her habituation to the disbelief she was in turned her away; and He made that clear by His saying ﴿إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾.
Yaʿlā ibn Muslim said: I read to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr ﴿إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ﴾, and he said: أَنَّها with fatḥa; and he said: He is only describing her, and is not beginning a new sentence.
There is another statement about its meaning: that the meaning is: and he (Sulaymān) turned her away from what she used to worship [Translator's note: the source reads تبعد, evidently for تعبد] besides Allah; then "عَنْ" was omitted, as prepositions are omitted with a verb that takes two objects, one of them via a preposition.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِي ٱلصَّرْحَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It was a pool of water which Sulaymān covered with glass.
Qatāda said: It was of glass with water behind it.
﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً﴾ i.e. water.
And it was said: «الصرح» is the palace — from Abū ʿUbayda — as he said:
* تَحْسِبُ أَعلاَمَهُنَّ الصُّرُوحَا *
(you would think their landmarks were lofty palaces)
And it was said: «الصرح» is the courtyard, as is reported: هذه صَرْحةُ الدَّارِ and قاعتُها with one meaning (this is the courtyard of the house).
Abū ʿUbayd related in al-Gharīb al-Muṣannaf that «الصرح» is every high, lofty building, and that al-mumarrad is the tall.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is that everything made of one material is called «صرح», from their saying لبَنٌ صَريحٌ (pure milk), when no water has been mixed with it; and from their saying صَرَّحَ بالأمرِ (he declared the matter openly); and from it: عربيٌّ صريح (a pure Arab).
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الصرح» al-mumarrad is the smooth, taken from the Arabs' saying: شَجَرةٌ مَرْداءُ, when its leaves have fallen from it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: And تمرَّد الرجل, when a man's beard is slow to appear after he has reached maturity.
Someone else said: And from it: رَمْلةٌ (مرداء), when sand grows nothing, and رجلٌ أمْرَدُ (a beardless man).
And it was said: al-mumarrad is the elongated; and from it some fortresses were called Mārid.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. believer and disbeliever. He said: and the dispute is their saying ﴿قَالُوا أَتَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ صالِحِاً مُرْسَلٌ مِنْ رَبِهِ﴾; this is the dispute.
And it was said: each party says: We are in the right.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. the punishment before the mercy.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: the disbelieving party sought to hasten the punishment, so Ṣāliḥ said to them: Why do you seek to hasten evil before good?.. ﴿لَوْلاَ تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ ٱللَّهَ﴾ i.e. why do you not seek Allah's forgiveness?

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ وَبِمَن مَّعَكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿اطَّيَّرَنَا﴾ i.e. we have taken an evil omen.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ طَائِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. the matter that befell you is with Allah;
i.e. the matter belongs to Allah; He afflicted you with it because of what your hands sent forth.
And it was said: the punishment for what you took as an evil omen is with Allah and will overtake you.
And it was said: ﴿طَائِرُكُمْ﴾ is what falls to your lot.
﴿بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ﴾ i.e. you are being tested.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانَ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ يُصْلِحُونَ﴾.
Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān said: Mālik ibn Dīnār recited this verse and said: How many in every clan and tribe are there of those who cause corruption?
ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said: It has reached me that they used to clip the dirhams.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ تَقَاسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: They swore to one another to attack Ṣāliḥ treacherously by night; so they went along "embracing one another" — i.e. hurrying — and Allah sent a rock upon them which destroyed them.
Mujāhid said: They swore to one another to come to Ṣāliḥ by night, and they were destroyed, and their people perished, all of them.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلُوطاً إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
i.e. and remember Lūṭ, or: and We sent Lūṭ.
Then He said ﴿أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾, i.e. while you see, i.e. you know that it is an abomination; so that makes your sin greater.
And it was said: some of you see that from others, and do not conceal it from one another.
Mujāhid said about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾: i.e. (they keep themselves pure) from the backsides of men and women — (said) in mockery of them.
Qatāda said: By Allah, they reproached them without any fault, for they kept themselves pure from evil deeds.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾.
Al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr narrated from al-Suddī, and Wakīʿ and Abū ʿĀṣim (narrated) from Sufyān: ﴿وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ﴾ — they both said: the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, whom Allah chose for His Prophet ﷺ.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
There is no good in what they associate (with Him); so the meaning is: Is the reward of Allah better, or the reward of what they associate?
Another answer, better than this, is that the meaning is: Is the good in this, or in this that they associate with Him in worship? As he said:
أَتَهْجُوهُ وَلَسْتَ لَهُ بِكُفْءٍ * فَشَرُّكُمَا لِخَيْرِكُمَا الفِدَاءُ
(Do you satirise him when you are no match for him? May the worse of you two be ransom for the better!)
And Sībawayh related: "Is happiness dearer to you, or misery?"
while he knows that happiness is dearer to him.
And the meaning is: Is what you associate with Allah better, or the One who guides you in the darknesses of land and sea when you have lost the way?

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾.
i.e. they deviate from the right course and the truth.
And it may be that the meaning is: they set up equals with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: beautiful date palms.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is from their saying: حُدِقَ بهِ, i.e. he was surrounded, as he said:
............. وَقَدْ حَدَقَتْ * بيَ المَنِيَّةُ وَاسْتَبْطَأْتُ أَنْصَارِي
(… when death had surrounded me, and I found my helpers slow to come.)

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ ٱدَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
And one says: بل ادَّرَك, i.e. it became complete, because they saw the realities with their own eyes.
Shuʿba narrated from Abū Jamra, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read ﴿بَلَى أَدَّارَكَ﴾? with fatḥa on the hamza as an interrogative, and with doubling of the dāl, ﴿عِلْمُهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, and said: i.e. it did not attain.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: i.e. it was absent.
And what is known of his reading is ﴿بَلَى ادَّارَكَ﴾, i.e. it followed in succession: they say, it will be and it will not be, and it will be at such-and-such a time.
Abū Jaʿfar said: In "آدَّارَكَ" here is the alif of reproachful questioning (tawqīf), i.e. "Has their knowledge in this world attained the reality of the Hereafter?" i.e. it has not attained (it); and sometimes the like of this comes without the interrogative alif.
Ibn Muḥayṣin read: "بل أآدَّرَكَ علمهُم", and Abū ʿAmr rejected this, saying: because only an affirmation occurs after "بَلْ".
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is permissible, with the meaning being: rather their knowledge did not attain (it), and rather this is said to them.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. it has come quickly upon you.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās about His saying ﴿رَدِفَ لكُمْ﴾: i.e. it has drawn near to you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is from رَدِفه, when he followed him and came in his track; and the lām was inserted because the meaning is: it has drawn near to you and come close to you; or it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم﴾.
i.e. it became due.
Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. the wrath fell upon them.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةً مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿تَكْلَمُهُمْ﴾ (it will wound them).
Abū Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr read ﴿تَكْلِمُهُمْ﴾, and Ubayy read "تُنَبِّئُهُمْ" (it will inform them).
Ibrāhīm said: The Beast will come out of Mecca.
Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated from Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān, who said: "The Beast will come out three times: once in the desert, then it will hide; once in the towns, in which the commanders will fight one another until bloodshed becomes abundant; and once from the best, noblest and greatest of mosques — until we thought he would name the Sacred Mosque, but he did not name it. The people will flee, and a small group of Muslims will remain. It will come out and make their faces shine; then no fugitive will escape it and no pursuer will catch it. It will come to a man while he is praying and say to him: Do you seek protection in prayer? And it will mark him; it will brand the face of the disbeliever and make the face of the believer shine."

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُواْ فَهُمْ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ﴾.
ʿAṭiyya narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: That is when they do not enjoin what is right and do not forbid what is wrong.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barāthī narrated to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: he said: Jibrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death.
And al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar al-Kūfī narrated to us; he said: Hannād ibn al-Sarī narrated to us; he said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿUmāra ibn Abī Ḥafṣa, from Ḥujr al-Hajarī, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, about His saying ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: he said: They are the martyrs; they are Allah's exception (thaniyya), girded with swords around the Throne.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَاخِرِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. humbled.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ﴾.
Because they have been crumbled and gathered together.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: (It is) "There is no god but Allah."
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾ — he said: "There is no god but Allah"; ﴿فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا﴾ — good will reach him; ﴿ومَنْ جَاءَ بالسَّيئةِ﴾ — and it is polytheism — ﴿فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُم في النَّارِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qays ibn Saʿd said: ﴿مَنْ جَاءَ بالحَسَنَةِ﴾ — with "There is no god but Allah"; ﴿ومَنْ جَاءَ بالسيِّئة﴾ — polytheism.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We do not know anyone of the exegetes who said other than this.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا﴾.
i.e. in yourselves and elsewhere.
